brief: Reid frames the summer yield sell-off as another leg of the post-Covid normalisation trade rather than a fiscal story: pressure for higher yields persists, but coupon income is holding returns up, so outright negative government bond returns are getting harder over the medium term. Last week energy drove the tape. No progress on the Strait of Hormuz sent Brent up 7.80% to $96.28/bbl and European gas up 7.42% in a fourth straight weekly gain, inflation fears pushed 10yr yields to multi-year highs (Bund 3.34%, US 4.78%), and risk assets struggled, with the STOXX 600 down 0.81% and credit spreads wider. Friday's +162k payrolls and +55k of revisions lifted priced odds of a September Fed hike to 62%. DB forecasts August headline CPI at +0.38% month-on-month on Friday and core at +0.21%, leaving headline 3.38% year-on-year and core 2.38%, and expects a 25bp ECB hike to 2.50% Thursday with another in December. The AfD took about 44% in Saxony-Anhalt against the CDU's 17%. Overnight, tech lifts Asia (KOSPI +4.18%) with US markets shut for Labor Day.
